kultivator.technique.titah_pedang.desc: A sword of Heaven's decree falls point-first down a pillar of light onto your crosshair. The land splits both ways along your aim and the sword stays planted where it struck.
kultivator.technique.titah_pedang.source: Source: inspired by Pangu separating heaven and earth (Sanwu Liji, Xu Zheng, 3rd century; the text names no weapon). The Decree Sword and the Celestial Court as its setting are game design (the Lingxiao Hall of Journey to the West).
kultivator.technique.titah_pedang.lore: What heaven has divided, no one joins again.
kultivator.technique.titah_tiang.desc: You hurl the iron pillar into heaven. It comes back down in silence; the boom follows, a shock ring flattens the land into a molten crater, and the pillar keeps standing in it.
kultivator.technique.titah_tiang.source: Source: Journey to the West ch. 3: the treasury of the East Sea Dragon King holds the divine iron that fixed the bottom of the Heavenly River, the pillar Yu the Great used to set the depth of rivers and seas when he tamed the flood. It began to glow when Sun Wukong came; that is the Ruyi Jingu Bang. Throwing the pillar from the sky, the molten crater and pulling it out again are game design.
kultivator.technique.titah_tiang.lore: The sea grew still the day it was set down.
kultivator.technique.titah_bintang: Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper
kultivator.technique.titah_bintang.desc: The Dipper is drawn onto the land. Its seven stars fall in order, star crystals grow where they land, and then every line between them ignites into a burning trench of light.
kultivator.technique.titah_bintang.sourc: Source: Beidou, the seven stars of the Northern Dipper: Tianshu, Tianxuan, Tianji, Tianquan, Yuheng, Kaiyang, Yaoguang. In the Soushen Ji (Gan Bao, 4th century) Guan Lu explains that the Southern Dipper rules life and the Northern Dipper rules death. The Shangqing school walks the Dipper's stars (bugang). The falling stars, the crystals and the burning trenches are game design.
kultivator.technique.titah_bintang.lore: The Northern Dipper keeps the ledger of death.
kultivator.technique.titah_gunung.desc: A square jade seal stamps the land. A light grid cuts it into cells, heaven carries the cells off into the sky, and a stepped, glowing pit is left behind. Foes in the square are lifted, then slammed down.
kultivator.technique.titah_gunung.source: Source: inspired by the Liezi, chapter Tang Wen: the Lord of Heaven, moved by the sincerity of Yu Gong (the Foolish Old Man), ordered the two sons of the Kua'e clan to carry the two mountains away. The giants, the jade seal, the light grid and the stepped pit are game design.
kultivator.technique.titah_gunung.lore: Sincerity moves heaven; heaven moves mountains.
item.kultivator.heaven_decree_seal.lore: A square white-jade seal with a gold cord and a coiled dragon, carved with 敕 ("by decree").
item.kultivator.heaven_decree_seal.sourc: Source: the Segel Titah Langit is game design; the decree of Heaven carried by the Heaven General follows the Heavenly Wrath (Panglima Langit).
